title: Build the full emergency fund: 3–6 months of essential expenses
summary: Sized to job-market liquidity in your industry and the variability of your income.
detailsHtml:
Sizing logic

Three months is the floor for stable W-2 income in a deep job market (tech in major hubs, healthcare, education). Six months is appropriate for narrower job markets, specialized roles, or single-earner households. For W-2 employees in cyclical industries (construction, hospitality, manufacturing), bias toward six months or more.

What counts as "essential expenses"

This is housing, utilities, food, insurance premiums, minimum debt payments, transportation, and minimum healthcare costs — not your full lifestyle. If you're laid off, you're not eating out, you're not on vacation, you're not contributing to retirement. The EF needs to cover the survival number, not the comfort number.

The Roth IRA backstop: Contributions (not earnings) to a Roth IRA can be withdrawn at any age, penalty-free and tax-free, because they were already taxed at contribution. This means a fully-funded Roth IRA functions as a deep secondary emergency reserve. Many people use this fact to keep their EF at the lower end of the recommended range and route additional savings to retirement instead.

Where to hold it

HYSA at 4–5% APY, money market funds, or short-term Treasury bills (which avoid state income tax). Not invested in equities. Not in a checking account. The EF's job is liquidity preservation, not return generation.
